lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Pinaceae through resinous woody habit, needle fascicles and free woody cone scales bearing two exposed ovules/seeds, then split the two project pines by fascicle/needle/cone/bark characters.

project_scope.selection_mode: Pinus echinata + Pinus taeda project module
project_scope.note: Both project species are accepted under current Kew and native to Texas. Exact target-zone nativity remains species-lane work.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the needles and their attachment. In project Pinus, foliage needles occur in fascicles enclosed at the base by a sheath. Then inspect the woody seed cone.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Resinous woody gymnosperms. In Pinus, long shoots bear short shoots/fascicles with 2–5 needles; project species use mostly 2 or 2–3 needles per fascicle.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: No flowers or fruits. Separate pollen cones and seed cones occur on the same tree in the project pines. Woody seed-cone scales are free from their subtending bracts for most of their length and usually bear 2 ovules/seeds on the upper surface.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Needles in fascicles + woody free-scaled seed cone = project Pinaceae/Pinus.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: needle fascicle → sheath → woody cone scale → exposed seeds → P. echinata vs P. taeda → Cupressaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: The biggest visual split from local junipers is immediate: pine needles are bundled in fascicles, while juniper foliage is scale-like or awl-like.

steps.title: 1 · Count needles per fascicle
steps.look_for: Needles grouped on a short shoot inside a persistent basal sheath.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the fastest Pinus architecture cue.

steps.title: 2 · Open the woody seed cone
steps.look_for: Spirally arranged woody scales, each associated with usually two seeds; scales are not fused into the fleshy/coalesced cone seen in Juniperus.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirms gymnosperm seed-cone architecture and separates Pinaceae from Cupressaceae.

steps.title: 3 · Shortleaf pine door
steps.look_for: Usually 2 needles per fascicle, about 7–11 cm; smaller 4–6 cm cones; older bark commonly shows resin pockets.
steps.why_it_matters: Best project suite against loblolly pine.

steps.title: 4 · Loblolly pine door
steps.look_for: Usually 2–3 needles per fascicle, generally 12–18 cm; larger 6–12 cm cones; bark lacks the characteristic shortleaf resin pockets.
steps.why_it_matters: Gives a whole-character suite rather than one-number ID.

steps.title: 5 · Joey Cupressaceae anchor
steps.look_for: Juniperus virginiana scale foliage at 19:20 in the Ft. Worth prairie video versus Pinus fascicled needles.
steps.why_it_matters: Uses an authoritative saved field frame to teach the Pinaceae-vs-Cupressaceae foliage split.

comparisons.title: Pinaceae vs Cupressaceae
comparisons.rule: Project Pinus has needles in fascicles and classic woody free-scaled cones. Juniperus has opposite/whorled scale or awl foliage and coalesced fleshy seed cones.

comparisons.title: Pinaceae vs Ginkgoaceae
comparisons.rule: Pinaceae has needle leaves and true seed cones; Ginkgo has broad fan leaves with dichotomous veins and naked ovules/seeds borne on stalks rather than in a cone.

comparisons.title: P. echinata vs P. taeda
comparisons.rule: Use the suite: shortleaf usually 2 shorter needles + smaller cones + bark resin pockets; loblolly usually 2–3 longer needles + larger cones. Hybrids occur, so avoid single-character certainty.

visual_lesson.caveat: Pinus echinata and P. taeda hybridize. Needle count and length overlap; species-level calls should use multiple characters.

genera.fast_cue: fascicled needles + persistent sheath + woody seed cone

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted by current Kew; native range includes Texas.
